rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Matter has wavelength h/p. Electrons accelerated through V volts have λ about 12.27/√V angstroms, short enough at 100 V to diffract from a crystal. Heavier everyday objects have wavelengths too small to notice. The wave describes probability, and the particle is still detected whole.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "De Broglie wavelength and matter waves" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
λ = h / p
λ = h / √(2 m e V) for an electron accelerated through V

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: De Broglie proposed that matter has a wavelength λ = h / p, where p is the momentum and h is Planck's constant. A faster or heavier particle has a shorter wavelength.  ·  For an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference V, (1/2) m v^2 = e V, so p = √(2 m e V) and λ = h / √(2 m e V).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Matter wave  ·  Momentum  ·  Electron wavelength  ·  Davisson–Germer

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Every particle has a wavelength.  ·  A larger momentum means a shorter wavelength.  ·  The electron is the usual classroom particle.  ·  The wave is a probability wave, not a sound wave.

rows.label: Universal facts

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: In angstroms a useful electron form is λ ≈ 12.27 / √V when V is in volts. At 100 V the wavelength is about 1.23 Å, the size of atomic spacings, which is why electron diffraction is visible.  ·  A cricket ball has a tiny wavelength because its momentum is huge. Its wave nature is real and undetectable. The effect shows up for electrons, neutrons and atoms.  ·  Davisson and Germer diffracted electrons from a nickel crystal and found the wavelength that de Broglie predicted. That is the experimental anchor.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A larger speed means a shorter wavelength, not a longer one.  ·  The angstrom formula is for electrons, not for protons.  ·  The wave is not a mechanical ripple.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: h/p uses momentum, not kinetic energy, unless you have converted.  ·  Use p = mv only when the speed is well below light.  ·  Name the particle before using the 12.27 formula.

rows.label: More ideas
